For 40 years, business orthodoxy said conglomerates don't work. Focus or die.

Then Musk built Tesla, SpaceX, xAI, Neuralink, X, Boring Company and Starlink, all profitable or pre-profit at scale, all sharing engineering talent, all reinforcing each other's missions.

It turns out the conglomerate model works fine. You just need engineering-led leadership and a unified mission.

Grok just got Connectors. Here's what changes.

Until now, every AI assistant existed in a sandbox. You'd ask a question, it would answer based only on what you typed in. Anything else, you had to copy-paste in yourself.

Connectors break the sandbox. Grok can now pull live context from:
Gmail ~ GitHub ~ Google Calendar ~ Notion ~ Google Drive ~ your own custom connectors

What you can do:
~ Summarize your inbox without forwarding anything 
~ Prep you for tomorrow's meetings using your actual calendar and recent emails 
~ Analyze a repo without you pasting code 
~ Pull insights from your Notion or Drive without leaving the chat
You ask. 

Grok pulls what it needs. The answer arrives.

This is the line where AI stops being a tool you use and starts being an assistant that knows your work.

xAI and SpaceX just signed a major partnership with Anthropic. 

Anthropic will use Colossus xAI’s massive supercluster with over 220,000 NVIDIA GPUs to train and run Claude AI models.

They’re also teaming up to explore building huge AI data centers in space. 

Why? Earth is running out of power, land, and cooling for these giant systems. 
SpaceX’s rockets could make orbital AI compute possible.

This move helps xAI make money from its extra compute power while pushing AI to the next level.

The future of AI might not just be on Earth anymore!

xAI, Google and Microsoft are giving the U.S. early access to new AI models.

The companies will share their latest systems with the government for preliminary national security risk checks before public release. It’s a coordinated move to get ahead of potential misuse and capability risks.

They’re working with CAISI on early evaluations, and more than 40 assessments have already been completed. The focus is on what these models can do and where they might create security concerns.

This signals a shift toward tighter collaboration between AI labs and government as models get more powerful.

SpaceX is going all-in on chips! 

The company has filed plans for a massive $55 billion initial investment (scaling up to $119 billion) in a next-generation, vertically integrated semiconductor and advanced computing fab in Grimes County, Texas — right between Austin and Houston.

This marks a huge move into domestic chip manufacturing as SpaceX expands far beyond rockets and satellites. A public hearing for property tax abatement is set for June 3, 2026.

America’s most ambitious company is now betting big on American semiconductor independence. What a time to be alive!
